title: AQA GCSE English Tuition Online: Language, Literature & Exam Technique
description: AQA-specific online GCSE English tuition for Language and Literature, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 exam technique, analytical writing and targeted feedback.

children: AQA GCSE English tuition is most useful when it targets the exact decisions students need to make in Language and Literature exams. The aim is not simply to complete more papers; it is to make the assessment method clear enough that the student can apply it independently.
AQA English Language: question-by-question support

Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward different combinations of comprehension, analysis, structure, evaluation, comparison and writing. Tuition can isolate one weak question type, model the thinking behind it, and then move from supported examples to independent timed practice.
Paper 1 Question 2: selecting precise language evidence and developing effects rather than feature spotting.
Paper 1 Question 3: tracking structural movement across the text rather than listing structural devices.
Paper 1 Question 4: building a judgement and supporting it with evaluative analysis.
Paper 1 Question 5: controlling ideas, structure, vocabulary and technical accuracy in creative writing.
Paper 2 Questions 2–4: inference, language analysis and comparison across non-fiction sources.
Paper 2 Question 5: adapting argument, register and structure to purpose, audience and form.

AQA English Literature

Literature support should combine secure knowledge of the set text with the ability to build a relevant argument. Learning quotations matters, but students also need to understand where evidence fits, what it proves and how to respond to the wording of the question rather than reproducing a memorised essay.
Build concise quotation banks around characters, themes and relationships.
Practise turning a quotation into an analytical claim rather than retelling the plot.
Develop introductions and topic sentences that answer the exact question.
Use context selectively where it genuinely illuminates the text.
Compare poetry through a clear line of argument instead of alternating disconnected paragraphs.
What a diagnostic lesson should establish

Before deciding the sequence of tuition, it is useful to identify whether the main barrier is knowledge, analysis, written expression, timing, technical accuracy or exam-question interpretation. Two students with the same mock grade may need completely different teaching.
How progress becomes visible

Look for stronger evidence choices, more precise explanations, clearer paragraph control, improved timing and fewer repeated errors. A student should gradually need less prompting to produce the same quality of response.

Is AQA-specific tuition the right fit?

If the student is studying AQA and the main problem is turning knowledge into marks, targeted question-level practice can be more efficient than generic English worksheets. Bring recent school work or mock responses where possible so the starting point is based on evidence.
